rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prisoners' visions foreshadow one man's rescue and the other's destruction; their questioning asks for the visions' interpretation.
rows.anchor: نجاة أحدكما وهلاك الآخر ومعنى استفتائهما فيه سؤالهما عنه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the two prisoners feigned dreams to test Joseph; after he interpreted them, they said they had been playing and had seen nothing.
rows.anchor: ما رأى صاحبا يوسف شيئا إنما تحالما ليجربا علمه

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: An unnamed investigator says the settled matter is the dreams themselves, not the men's eventual fates, because an inquiry seeks an answer about an incident, not its outcome.
rows.anchor: ذهب بعض المحققين إلى أن المراد به ما رأياه من الرؤيتين ونفى أن يكون المراد ما يؤول إليه أمرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The investigator argues that asking for interpretation means asking about the dreams as events, analogizing the king's request to be advised about his dream.
rows.anchor: لأن الإستفتاء إنما يكون في الحادثة لا في حكمها

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: He reads the wording as magnifying the dreams: the text calls them an affair and their request an inquiry because such inquiry concerns obscure, momentous cases; the present tense prolongs the request until Joseph finishes answering.
rows.anchor: وعبر عن ذلك بالأمر وعن طلب تأويله بالإستفتاء تهويلا لأمره وتفخيما لشأنه

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: He explains the singular 'matter' despite two dreams as matching the prisoners' own singular wording, and says they asked about the image of the outcome rather than their crime or its cause.
rows.anchor: على حسب ما وحداه في قولهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi objects that the investigator's distinction between the matter and the event is inconsistent: if the outcome and dream are treated as identical for predication, they can also be identical for inquiry.
rows.anchor: بعد اعتبار العينية بين شيئين يكون صحة نسبة ما هو من أحوال أحدهما إلى الآخر

rows.speaker: الكثير
rows.claim: Many exegetes take the matter as the men's eventual outcome and understand the preposition causally: they asked about the dreams in order to learn their fate; Al-Alusi finds this the stronger, less strained reading.
rows.anchor: ويرجح ما ذهب إليه الكثير أن فيه سلامة من نزع الخف قبل الوصول إلى الماء

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view takes the matter as the crime for which the men were accused and imprisoned, supplying an omitted noun meaning the consequence of that accusation.
rows.anchor: المراد بالأمر ما اتهما به والكلام حينئذ على حذف مضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report of Joseph's answer may be a rebuttal to the prisoners' denial or a confirmation of his interpretation; a lie by the cupbearer could have protected his companion, and another report says the baker was the one who denied it.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون للرد عليهما حسبما ورد في الأثر يحتمل أن يكون تحقيقا لتعبيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The episode is cited for the maxim that dreams occur as first interpreted, expressed in the saying that a dream rests on a bird's wing until told, then falls.
rows.anchor: المنام على جناح طائر إذا قص وقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect 'he thought' emphasizes certainty that one prisoner would be saved and prepares for Joseph's request to be remembered; some early authorities instead identify the saved man as the one who thought so.
rows.anchor: أوثِر على صيغة المضارع مبالغة في الدلالة على تحقيق النجاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph is the one who knows the prisoner's rescue; here ظن means certainty, as in the verse about those certain they will meet their Lord.
rows.anchor: والظان هو يوسف عليه السلام لأصحابه وإن ذهب إليه بعض السلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Joseph's certainty ظن may be deferential etiquette toward God; alternatively it reflects interpretation by inference, supporting the view that dream interpretation is conjectural rather than certain.
rows.anchor: ولعل التعبير به من باب إرخاء العنان والتأدب مع الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'among them' can modify saved or be circumstantial, but cannot attach to 'saved' as its complement because that does not fit the intended meaning.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون متعلقا بناج لأنه ليس المعنى عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph asks the rescued cupbearer to mention him to his master, including the state and qualities the cupbearer had witnessed.
rows.anchor: بما أنا عليه من الحال والصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that on the third day, at the prison gate, the cupbearer asked Joseph for his need; Joseph asked him to describe him to the king, but Satan distracted the man until he forgot.
rows.anchor: إلى باب السجن قال له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forgotten remembrance is Joseph's mention before the king, not remembrance of God; the genitive can mean remembering Joseph, or reporting him to his master.
rows.anchor: أي ذكر يوسف عليه السلام عند الملك والإضافة لأدنى ملابسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The causal ف links the lapse to Joseph's request, since seeking human assistance was the occasion of the rescued man's forgetting.
rows.anchor: والفاء للسببية فإن توصيته عليه السلام المتضمنة للإستعانة بغيره سبحانه وتعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بضع is commonly three to nine; Qatada says three to nine, Mujahid three to seven, and Abu Ubayda one to ten. Al-Farra says it accompanies tens, not hundreds or thousands; the word derives from cutting.
rows.anchor: البضع ما بين الثلاث إلى التسع كما روي عن قتادة وعن مجاهد أنه من الثلاث إلى السبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most accounts make Joseph's whole imprisonment seven years, with two years after the request to the cupbearer; another view makes the post-request stay seven years after five earlier years, totaling twelve.
rows.anchor: وهي مدة لبثه كلها فيما صححه البعض وسنتان منها كانت مدة لبثه بعد ذلك القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report claiming seven additional years after five is not established in that wording; the versions judged established merely say Joseph remained imprisoned as long as he remained.
rows.anchor: الخبر لم يثبت بهذا اللفظ وإنما الثابت في عدة روايات ما لبث في السجن طول ما لبث

rows.speaker: طاوس والضحاك
rows.claim: Tawus and al-Dahhak, as cited by Ibn Hatim, explain this occurrence of بضع as fourteen years, an uncommon interpretation.
rows.anchor: روي ابن حاتم عن طاوس والضحاك تفسير البضع ههنا بأربع عشرة سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi advises against assigning the prison term an exact number, despite the divergent reports.
rows.anchor: والأولى أن لا يجوز بمقدار معين كما قدمنا

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports that God reminded Joseph of being saved from his brothers, the well, and the woman, then asked why he forgot God and remembered a human; Joseph said it was only a word spoken by his tongue, and God swore to confine him for several years.
rows.anchor: من استنقذك من القتل حين هم إخوتك أن يقتلوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although seeking help from people in hardship is generally permissible, as cooperation in righteousness shows, what suits prophets is to leave that concession and choose the higher resolve.
rows.anchor: واللائق بمناصب الأنبياء عليهم السلام ترك ذلك والأخذ بالعزائم

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says Joseph asked the cupbearer to remember him in order to guide the king to faith, not to secure his release; Al-Alusi calls this contrary to the apparent sense and reports, though fitting Joseph's rank.
rows.anchor: واختار أبو حيان أن يوسف عليه السلام إنما قال للشرابي ما قال ليتوصل بذلك إلى هداية الملك وإيمانه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take both pronouns in 'Satan made him forget his lord' to refer to Joseph; forgetfulness here means leaving the better course for a spiritual elite, not Satanic misguidance.
rows.anchor: ترك الأولى بالنسبة لمقام الخواص الرافعين للأسباب من البين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi favors the usual reading in which the rescued cupbearer forgets Joseph before the king, since it suits the causal ف and the later mention of remembering after a long time.
rows.anchor: الأول هو المناسب لكان الفاء ولقوله تعالى الآتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king is Rayyan, who was an unbeliever; his title illustrates the permissibility of calling an unbeliever king, though some prohibit king or amir for fear the title implies rightfulness, citing Muhammad's letter to Heraclius as 'great Roman'.
rows.anchor: الريان وكان كافرا ففي إطلاق ذلك عليه دلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king's 'I see' means 'I saw'; the present tense vividly recounts the past vision.
rows.anchor: أي رأيت وإيثار صيغة المضارع لحكاية الحال الماضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سمان describes cows full of flesh and fat; the plural can be regular as in كريم/كرام, and its lexical forms derive from samāna and samn.
rows.anchor: ممتلئات لحما وشحما من سمن كسمع سمانة بالفتح وسمنا كعنبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect 'they eat' means that they ate, but makes the strange scene present to the listener; the clause is circumstantial or adjectival.
rows.anchor: أي أكلهن والعدول إلى المضارع لاستحضار الصورة تعجيبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عجاف means very thin. Its plural is عجفاء, unusually patterned as عجاف rather than the expected عجف; it is formed in opposition to سمان.
rows.anchor: أي سبع بقرات مهزولة جدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Describing the numeral's discriminator سمان rather than making it an adjective of the numeral better distinguishes by kind than gender and more fully removes ambiguity; a derived adjective is not a sound discriminator in formal usage.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكروا أنه إذا وصف التمييز كان التمييز بالنوع وإذا وصف المميز كان التمييز بالجنس

rows.speaker: صاحب الفرائد
rows.claim: The author of al-Fara'id objects that numeral discriminators normally appear in genitive construction: with seven lean, an omitted cows is needed, whereas adding lean could make the adjective stand for cows and avoid ellipsis.
rows.anchor: واعترض صاحب الفرائد بأن الأصل في العدد التمييز بالإضافة

rows.speaker: القطب
rows.claim: Al-Qutb replies that the preceding mention of seven cows already identifies the lean seven as cows, so إضافة عجاف would make an adjective do the work of a discriminator; treating it as standing for cows applies only when it is an adjective.
rows.anchor: تعقب ذلك القطب بأنه هب أن الأصل في العدد التمييز بالإضافة

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Tibi says describing the number before its discriminator stresses both count and quality, while naming the discriminator first makes the description the focus; omission in all three parallel images serves the scene's movement from ease to hardship.
rows.anchor: إن المميز إذا وصف ثم رفع به الإبهام والإجمال من العدد آذن بأنهما مقصودان في الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says the fat cows are named first because they appeared first: seven fat cows emerged from a dry river, then seven lean ones swallowed them without visibly changing.
rows.anchor: بأنه أول ما رأى السمان فقد روي أنه رأى سبع بقرات سمان خرجن من نهر يابس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The green ears had formed kernels and were green; the dry ears had ripened and curled until no green remained, according to a report. Their number is omitted because the earlier seven cows supply it.
rows.anchor: قد انعقد حبها واخضر أي وسبعا أخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects coordinating أخر with سنبلات: the seven would then be both the green ears and a different set of dry ears, a numerical contradiction; coordination with a single set of seven men divided between standing and sitting is different.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز عطف أخر على سنبلات لأن العطف على المميز يقتضي أن يكون المعطوف والمعطوف عليه بيانا للمعدود

rows.speaker: صاحب الفرائد
rows.claim: Al-Fara'id argues coordination normally repeats the numeral: seven other ears would then be added to seven green ones, making fourteen; under the alternative ellipsis analysis the reading would instead wrongly make all ears total seven.
rows.anchor: ونظر في ذلك صاحب الفرائد فقال : إن الصحيح أن العطف في حكم تكرير العامل

rows.speaker: صاحب الفرائد
rows.claim: Al-Fara'id further prefers coordinating with خضر rather than يابسات, so the dry description has an expressed ears noun and need not be supplied from context.
rows.anchor: وادعى أن الأولى أن يكون العطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says the objection still assumes a discriminator already fixed at seven; neither repetition nor ellipsis resolves that contradiction, and he prefers the ellipsis or 'withdrawal' analysis followed by Ibn al-Hajib.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك يظهر أنه لا مدخل للتكرير ولا الإنسحاب في هذا الفرض ثم إن المختار قول الإنسحاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that أخر would be needless under an omitted seven is unsound: both competing grammatical analyses are recognized as apparent by Arab grammarians, so the word can emphasize the intended reading rather than be verbose.
rows.anchor: فغير سديد على ما في الكشف لأن القائل بالتقدير يدعي الظهور في الإستقلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address يا أيها الملأ is to notables thought to possess knowledge; one report says the king gathered magicians, soothsayers, and dream interpreters.
rows.anchor: خطاب للأشراف ممن يظن به العلم يروى أنه جمع السحرة والكهنة والمعبرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king asks them to interpret the dream and state its consequence; another view says he addresses his companions and calls the task a fatwa to honor them and magnify the vision.
rows.anchor: أي عبروها وبينوا حكمها وما تؤول إليه من العاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dream interpretation is the habitual passage from a seen dream-image to its corresponding external or inward reality; عبور means crossing, and تأويل names what the dream comes to.
rows.anchor: وهي الإنتقال من الصورة المشاهدة في المنام إلى ما هي صورة ومثال لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light form عبر الرؤيا is more established and forceful in linguistic usage than the doubled form; although some deny the latter, al-Mubarrad's Bedouin poem attests it.
rows.anchor: عبرت الرؤيا بالتخفيف عبارة أقوى وأعرف عند أهل اللغة

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad cites a Bedouin poet's line about seeing and interpreting a dream as evidence that the doubled verb تعبير is attested.
rows.anchor: ما أنشده المبرد في الكامل لبعض الأعراب

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan takes the lām in للرؤيا as an emphatic or strengthening lām for a delayed weakened verb; other accounts call it explanatory, make it indicate eagerness to interpret, or treat الرؤيا as a predicate of كان, which Al-Alusi considers strained.
rows.anchor: وقيل واختاره أبو حيان إنها لتقوية الفعل المذكور لأنه ضعف بالتأخير

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Ja'far assimilates the hamza in الرؤيا after changing it to wāw and then yā because a preceding wāw is unvocalized; grammarians call this irregular because the wāw substitution is not obligatory.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر بالإدغام في الرؤيا وبابه بعد قلب الهمزة واوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The survivor is Joseph's cupbearer. Most read وادكر with dāl, from a form where t assimilated to d; al-Hasan reads اذكر with ذ assimilated to ذ, while the first reading is more eloquent. Both mean recalling Joseph.
rows.anchor: أي صاحبي يوسف عليه السلام وهو الشرابي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After a long interval, after umma means after a span or community of time.
rows.anchor: طائفة من الزمان ومدة طويلة

rows.speaker: الأشهب العقيلي
rows.claim: Al-Ashhab al-Uqayli reads إمة as a favor: release from the threat of execution and prison, and the king's beneficence toward the cupbearer; a verse illustrates this usage.
rows.anchor: بكسر الهمزة وتشديد الميم أي نعمة عليه بعد نعمة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya takes the favor as God's favor on Joseph by bringing his release near, but Al-Alusi considers this interpretation far-fetched.
rows.anchor: المراد بعد نعمة أنعم الله تعالى بها على يوسف عليه السلام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وزيد بن علي
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Zayd ibn Ali, Mujahid, Ikrima, and Shubayl ibn Azra are reported to read with a light, open form from a verb meaning to forget; Al-Alusi dismisses those who rejected this reading.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عباس وزيد بن علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase after a long time is parenthetical between the speech verb and its content; it could be circumstantial with an understood قد, but joining it to the relative clause is rejected because the later remembering is new information, not a known description.
rows.anchor: والجملة اعتراض بين القول والمقول وجوز أن تكون حالا من الموصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cupbearer offers to inform them through access to someone who knows the interpretation, not from his own knowledge; he says send me so they will dispatch him to Joseph.
rows.anchor: أي أخبركم بتأويل ذلك الذي خفى أمره بالتلقي ممن عنده علمه لا من تلقاء نفسي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads أنا آتيكم, 'I will bring you,' instead of 'I will inform you'; when corrected, he asks whether Joseph himself had been informing them.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم وأبو الشيخ عن الحسن أنه كان يقرأ أنا آتيكم

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy is also reported to read أنا آتيكم; al-Bahr says this is likewise the reading in the codex.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر وغيره عن أبي أنه قرأ أيضا كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural imperative send me can address only the king as an honorific plural; a report says the cupbearer knelt and asked that the king send him to a knowledgeable man in prison. Ibn Abbas says the prison was outside the king's city, while another view puts it inside; Al-Alusi leaves its actual location to God.
rows.anchor: وضمير الجمع إما لأنه أراد الملك وحده لكن خاطبه بذلك على سبيل التعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حفص reads دأبا with fatḥa and most with sukūn; a light alif form is also transmitted. It is a verbal noun of toil, extended to habitual persistence, and can be a circumstantial description of the cultivators or an absolute object of an omitted verb.
rows.anchor: قرأ حفص بفتح الهمزة والجمهور بإسكانها وقريء دابا بألف من غير همز

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad parses دأبا as an absolute object of تزرعون, like قعد القرفصاء; Al-Alusi rejects that analysis.
rows.anchor: وعند المبرد مفعول مطلق لتزرعون وذلك عنده نظير قعد القرفصاء وليس بشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph interprets the seven fat cows and green ears as seven fertile years and the lean cows and dry ears as seven famine years, during which they should cultivate diligently.
rows.anchor: وقد أول عليه السلام البقرات السمان والسنبلات الخضر بسنين مخاصيب

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some read تزرعون as an imperative to cultivate, cast as a report to make fulfillment sound already accomplished; the harvest instruction would then also be imperative.
rows.anchor: المراد الأمر بالزراعة كذلك فالجملة خبر لفظا أمر معنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to leave grain in its ears prevents weevils from consuming it; Egyptian grain stores can be ruined after roughly two years, and the green ears may suggest this storage counsel is another imperative.
rows.anchor: فذروه في سنبله ولا تذروه كيلا يأكله السوس كما هو شأن غلال مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians object that an imperative harvest instruction cannot coordinate with a declarative forecast; replies treat it as independent advice, an answer to an implied condition, or understand the imperative as a report because it is Joseph's guidance.
rows.anchor: لأنه لو لم يؤول ذلك بالأمر لزم عطف الإنشاء على الخبر

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf finds the strongest reading predictive: the cultivation forecast interprets the dream, while the storage instruction interrupts it as urgent advice, making what will happen seem already present.
rows.anchor: على أصله لأنه تأويل المنام بدليل قوله الآتي

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: If تزرعون is instead an imperative, some treat the storage instruction as part of the dream's interpretation because the lean cows and dry ears predict eating what the fertile years produced; others regard it as advice outside the interpretation.
rows.anchor: أن ما حصدتم الخ على تقدير كون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They should leave all but the small amount needed to eat during the fertile years; the advice encourages moderation in food.
rows.anchor: أي اتركوا ذلك في السنبل إلا ما لا غنى عنه من القليل الذي تأكلونه

rows.speaker: السلمي
rows.claim: Al-Sulami reads مما يأكلون with yā, meaning what people eat, rather than addressing the audience as 'you'.
rows.anchor: وقرأ السلمي مما يأكلون بالياء على الغيبة أي يأكل الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seed grain is not separately excepted because the command to cultivate seven years already makes retaining seed understood.
rows.anchor: والاقتصار على استثناء المأكول دون البذر لكون ذلك معلوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven difficult years follow the seven named years; saying 'after that' rather than 'after them' magnifies the preceding period. 'Seven' is understood as years from the earlier wording.
rows.anchor: من بعد السنين السبع المذكورات وإنما لم يقل من بعدهن قصدا إلى تفخيم شأنهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The famine years consume the grain stored for them; attributing eating to years is figurative for what people undergo, and لهن reinforces that personification or matches the dream's imagery.
rows.anchor: وإسناد الأكل إليهن مع أنه حال الناس فيهن مجازي

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some understand 'eating' as utterly exhausting or destroying, as in the idiom that a journey ate a camel's flesh.
rows.anchor: أكل السير لحم الناقة أي أفناه وذهب به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The small amount they preserve is what they protect and store for the next planting; the verb derives from the sense of a fortress as protection and refuge.
rows.anchor: أي تحرزونه وتخبئونه لبروز الزراعة مأخوذ من الحصن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عام and سنة both mean year, but عام often suggests ease and fertility whereas سنة often suggests hardship and famine; the positive term signals the changed conditions from the preceding years.
rows.anchor: هو كالسنة لكن كثيرا ما يستعمل فيما فيه الرخاء والخصب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والجمهور
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and most exegetes explain يغاث الناس as receiving rain, from the triliteral root غاث.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد والجمهور فهو من غاث الثلاثي اليائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation derives it from relief: God will succor them by lifting the hardships pressing upon them, using the fourth-form verb from غوث.
rows.anchor: أمدنا برفع المكاره حين أظلتنا فهو رباعي واوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will press products normally squeezed, such as grapes, sugarcane, olives, and sesame; explicit mention matters because rain does not ensure these crops as directly as grain, or because this special good news suits the king's own circumstances and makes his reading's second-person form apt.
rows.anchor: من العصر المعروف أي يعصرون ما من شأنه أي يعصر من العنب والقصب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the verb as milking; this can derive from pressing because milking squeezes the udder to release milk.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس تفسير ذلك بيحلبون وكأنه مأخوذ من العصر المعروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating فيه can signal different times or kinds of benefit, enumerate the year's blessings, or emphasize that the preceding drought's rain was negligible beside this year's; the fronting of the phrase marks the focus, with rhyme also possible for the second occurrence.
rows.anchor: المقام مقام تعداد منافع ذلك العام ولأجله قدم

rows.speaker: جعفر بن محمد والأعرج وعيسى البصرة
rows.claim: Ja'far ibn Muhammad, al-Aʿraj, and ʿIsa of Basra read يعصرون as passive; ʿIsa also transmits a second-person passive reading, 'you will be delivered' from hardship, matching 'people will receive rain'.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جعفر بن محمد رضي الله تعالى عنهما والأعرج وعيسى البصرة

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda and others take the active form as pressing in the sense of rescue; al-Bahr gives a related lexical sense of relief and cites Abu Zubayd's poem about Uthman as a refuge for the distressed.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي عبيدة وغيره أخذ المبني للفاعل من العصر بمعنى النجاة أيضا

rows.speaker: ابن المنير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Munir understands the verb as receiving rain from a cloud whose time to be squeezed has come, with the preposition omitted or the verb carrying the sense of raining.
rows.anchor: معناه عصيرون من أعصرت السحابة عليهم أي حان وقت عصر الرياح لها لتمطر

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawhari says عصر القوم means that a people received rain, which makes the reading apparent without a verbal supplement.
rows.anchor: وفي الصحاح عصر القوم أي أمطروا ومنه قراءة بعضهم

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqash transmits a doubled form يعصّرون with a passive yā and kasra on ṣād, conveying abundance or intensity.
rows.anchor: وحكى النقاش أنه قريء ( يعصرون ) بضم الياء وكسر الصاد وتشديدها

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads تعصرون with a doubled consonant from an assimilated form of تعتصرون; it can mean squeezing fruit or being rescued.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي رضي الله تعالى عنهما ( وفيه تعصرون ) بكسر التاء والعين والصاد

rows.speaker: قتادة وابن عباس
rows.claim: Qatada, as transmitted by Ibn Jarir and others, and Ibn Abbas say God granted Joseph knowledge of this year's details by revelation; Al-Alusi treats revelation as the apparent source.
rows.anchor: كما أخرج ابن جرير وغيره عن قتادة علم آتاه الله تعالى علمه لم يكن فيما سئل عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph ends his answer to the king with the glad news; unlike his answer to the prisoners, where the prediction came first, this placement at the end highlights his excellence.
rows.anchor: ولقد أتى عليه السلام بما يدل على فضله في آخر فتواه على عكس ما فعل أولا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A non-revelatory view says Joseph inferred that drought naturally ends in abundance or that God sends ease after hardship; Al-Alusi rejects it because the prophecy would be vague, especially in readings where mutual relief is described, which only revelation could establish.
rows.anchor: إن هذه البشارة منه عليه السلام لم تكن عن وحي بل لأن العادة جارية

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam reports Joseph began testing the coming famine by preparing two portions for each man; when one man ate all of his, Joseph said that was the first day of the hard years.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن زيد بن أسلم أنه عليه السلام كان بعد ذلك يصنع لرجل طعام اثنين

rows.speaker: البلخي
rows.claim: Al-Balkhi uses the counselors' dismissal of the king's dream as confused dreams to challenge the rule that dreams occur according to their first interpretation; Al-Alusi replies with the hadith that a dream hangs on a bird's wing until interpreted, and says dismissing it as meaningless may not count as interpretation.
rows.anchor: واستدل البلخي بتأويله لذلك على بطلان قول من يقول

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi restricts the dream rule to visions admitting several possible meanings: one interpretation is made and then comes to pass.
rows.anchor: إنه ينبغي أن يخص ذلك بما يحتمل من الرؤيا وجوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage is also cited as evidence that an unbeliever can have a true dream; interpreters are advised not to ask at sunrise, sunset, or night, and some say a dream seen in sleep is its own interpretation. Al-Alusi finds many such claims opaque.
rows.anchor: واستدلوا بذلك أيضا على صحة رؤيا الكافر وهو ظاهر وقد ذكروا للإستفتاء عن الرؤيا آدابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After hearing the full and precise interpretation, the king asks for Joseph because of his knowledge and virtue, which disclose what only God could make known.
rows.anchor: لما رأى من علمه وفضله وأخباره عما لا يعلمه إلا اللطيف الخبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the messenger who had been Joseph's fellow prisoner arrives to say the king wants him, Joseph tells him to return to his master, the king.
rows.anchor: وهو صاحبه الذي استفتاه وقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rather than explicitly ordering an investigation, Joseph asks the king what happened with the women; a question provokes the king's curiosity and concern for what he does not know, whereas a direct request might seem bold and be refused.
rows.anchor: وإنما لم يقل فاسأله أن يفتش عن ذلك حثا للملك على الجد في التفتيش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph omits the Aziz's wife, the principal party, out of courtesy and magnanimity, which moves her to confess; another explanation is that he feared her continued plotting, while expecting the other women to tell the truth.
rows.anchor: وإنما لم يتعرض السلال لامرأة العزيز مع أنها الأصيل لما لا قاه تأدبا وتكرما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By mentioning the women's cutting their hands without directly accusing them of seduction, Joseph is tactful, guards against their taking offense, and alludes to the events through his lord's knowledge of their guile.
rows.anchor: مجاملة معهن واحترازا عن سوء مقالتهن

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari offers three readings of 'my Lord knows their guile': it is too great for anyone but God to know; God knows they plotted and that Joseph is innocent; or it is a veiled warning that God knows and will punish them.
rows.anchor: وفي الكشاف أنه عليه السلام أراد بهذا أنه كيد عظيم لا يعلمه إلا الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first reading, reserving full knowledge of their guile to God adds suspense and urges the king to investigate; the sentence completes Joseph's request to inquire.
rows.anchor: زيادة تشويق وبعث إلى تعرف الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the second reading, the sentence sums up the case: if God knows the women plotted, Joseph is necessarily innocent. The third can serve either function and may stir the king to punish them, though that seems ill-matched to Joseph's nobility.
rows.anchor: وإذا كان كيدا يكون لا محالة بريئا والكيد هو الحدث وعلى الثالث تحتملهما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masud relates the Prophet's admiration for Joseph's nobility and patience: he said he would have required release before interpreting the dream and would have hurried out when summoned from prison, unlike Joseph's patient insistence on clarifying his innocence.
rows.anchor: لقد عجبت من يوسف وكرمه وصبره والله تعالى يغفر له حين سئل عن البقرات العجاف والسمان

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One explanation of the Prophet's prayer is that Joseph chose a concession rather than the higher resolve: he put clearing his name ahead of God's right to convey monotheism and the message.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى ترك العزيمة بالرخصة وهي تقديم حق الله تعالى بتبليغ التوحيد والرسالة

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Tibi reads the prayer as a respectful, conventional rebuke, like telling an honored person 'may God forgive you' while querying his answer.
rows.anchor: العلامة الطيبي من قبيل قولك لمن تعظمه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view says clearing his name served God's cause too: once the accusation was removed, Joseph's later teaching would be accepted; avoiding situations that invite suspicion is obligatory.
rows.anchor: إن في براءته النفس من حق الله تعالى ما فيها فإنها إذا تحققت عندهم وقع ما تلاها موقع القبول

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Muslim's report from Anas says the Prophet, walking with a wife, called out to a passerby that she was his wife; when the man said he would never suspect him, the Prophet explained that Satan circulates through humans like blood, illustrating the need to dispel suspicion.
rows.anchor: وأخرج مسلم من رواية أنس أن رسول الله عليه الصلاة والسلام كان مع إحدى نسائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari documented with judges that his leg was lost to frost on a journey, not crime, and displayed their letters in each town to prevent suspicion; Joseph may likewise have feared that silence would invite detractors to undermine his message.
rows.anchor: أن رجله لم تقطع في جناية ولا فساد بل سقطت من ثلج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi rejects Ibn Atiyya's suggestion that 'my lord' means the Aziz as in Joseph's earlier statement about his master, and rejects changing the antecedent of 'their guile' to women generally.
rows.anchor: وزعم ابن عطية أنه يحتمل أن يكون عليه السلام أراد بالرب العزيز

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة وأبو بكر
rows.claim: Abu Haywa and Abu Bakr in one transmission from Asim read النِّسوة with a rounded ḍamma on nūn; another group reads اللائي with yā, like the plural اللاء.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وأبو بكر عن عاصم في رواية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king's question is introduced as a continuation: what was the women's affair when they tried to seduce Joseph, and did they find that he inclined toward them? Their answer presupposes his total chastity.
rows.anchor: الأمر العظيم الذي يحق لعظمته أن يكثر فيه التخاطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women's حاشا لله expresses their amazement and declares Joseph's purity; the indefinite سوء with extra من emphatically denies every kind of wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: أجبن بجواب جيد يظهر منه براءة أنفسهن جملة

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf explains that the question first asks whether Joseph felt any inclination, which would be the beginning of his response to their advances; their answer marvels at God's creating such chastity and denies even a trace of misconduct.
rows.anchor: خافت أن يشهد عليها بما قالت يوم قطعن أيديهن

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the women answer well, clearing themselves fully and giving Joseph some vindication; Al-Alusi says that misses al-Kashf's account of the framing question and their words' limited scope.
rows.anchor: قاله الخليل وهو مأخوذ من الحصة وهي القطعة من الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Aziz's wife was present; one report says the women turned to press her, while another says fear that the women would repeat what she said when they cut their hands prompted her to confess.
rows.anchor: وإلى ذلك ذهب الزجاج أيضا

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil derives حصحص الحق from حصّة, a portion: the portion of truth became distinct from falsehood; al-Zajjaj agrees.
rows.anchor: من حص شعره إذا استأصله بحيث ظهرت بشرة رأسه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj also explains حصحص as separating the share of truth from the share of falsehood.
rows.anchor: قال حميد بن ثور الهلالي يصف بعيرا : فحصحص في صم الصفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another derivation connects حصحص to cropping hair until the scalp appears; a line attributed to a poet describes a shaved head, and this too returns to the sense of becoming visible.
rows.anchor: وذكر الراغب وغيره أن حص وحصحص ككف

rows.speaker: حميد بن ثور الهلالي
rows.claim: Humayd ibn Thawr al-Hilali uses حصحص for a camel settling its chest on hard rocks, supporting the sense that truth became firm and established.
rows.anchor: اسم للوقت الحاضر جميعه كوقت فعل الإنشاء حال النطق به

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib notes the reduplicated pattern حصحص alongside كفكف and كبكب; a passive reading means truth was set in its proper place.
rows.anchor: وذكر الراغب وغيره أن حص وحصحص ككف وكفكف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الآن denotes the current time, either the whole moment when an utterance is made or the part of the present represented here; another verse uses it in 'now God has lightened you'.
rows.anchor: اسم للوقت الحاضر جميعه كوقت فعل الإنشاء حال النطق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grammar and derivation of الآن are disputed: its alif is traced to wāw in أوان or to yā in آن يئين; a proposed original أوان with a deleted alif is rejected because wāw before alif does not normally change, while another analysis compares it to راح/رواح.
rows.anchor: وألفه منقلبة عن واو لقولهم في معناه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says الآن is built because it contains the meaning of a demonstrative, 'this time'; the objection is that demonstrative pronouns do not take the article.
rows.anchor: فقال الزجاج : بني لتضمنه معنى الإشارة

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali says الآن is built because it contains the meaning of the definite lam; Al-Alusi objects that an implied particle's meaning cannot sensibly be expressed by adding that very particle.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو علي : لتضمنه معنى لام التعريف

rows.speaker: المبرد وابن السراج والزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad, Ibn al-Sarraj, and al-Zamakhshari say الآن is built because it was originally indefinite but has used the article since its first use; Ibn Malik objects that other initially articulated phrases remain inflected, and that mere unusualness does not cause building.
rows.anchor: وقال المبرد وابن السراج : لأنه خالف نظائره

rows.speaker: ابن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Malik instead attributes building to الآن's fixed, particle-like form: unlike حين and وقت it cannot be dualized, pluralized, or diminished; Abu Hayyan objects to the argument.
rows.anchor: واختار أنه نبي لشبه الحرف في ملازمة لفظ واحد

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says الآن retains the building of the past verb آن, 'the time came'; the objection is that it takes the article, unlike that verb, and can be declined.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء : إنما بني لأنه نقل من فعل ماض

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some grammarians treat الآن as an inflected accusative of time, citing a poetic 'both full from now' with genitive nūn; critics reply that the vowel may be built kasra, and Ibn al-Sa'igh says those deriving it from أوان also treat that form as inflected.
rows.anchor: وذهب بعضهم إلى أنه معرب منصوب على الظرفية

rows.speaker: السيوطي
rows.claim: Al-Suyuti chooses to treat الآن as inflected and accusative in an adverbial role because no valid cause for building it has been established; its use outside that role is unproven.
rows.anchor: واختار الجلال السيوطي القول بإعرابه لأنه لم يثبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this sentence الآن modifies حصحص: truth became clear at the time she spoke.
rows.anchor: وأياما كان فهو هنا متعلق بحصحص أي حصحص الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Aziz's wife confesses that she seduced Joseph, not that he seduced her, to confirm his innocence; she may have confessed because denial was useless or because obsessive love made her indifferent to exposure.
rows.anchor: وإنما قالت ذلك بعد اعترافها تأكيدا لنزاهته عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two explanations are given for the Aziz wife’s confession: she knew denial would not work after the women testified, or her overwhelming love made her disregard exposure and shame.
rows.anchor: لم تبال بانتهاك سترها وظهور سرها

rows.speaker: إرشاد العقل السليم
rows.claim: Irshad says she means that the actual truth of the disputed incident and her betrayal have now become clear, not merely the women's limited testimony about Joseph's general innocence; now means the moment of her own statement, making even his adversaries attest to his purity.
rows.anchor: إرشاد العقل السليم أنها لم ترد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers' question is a confirmation-seeking expression of astonishment, hence emphatic إن and lām despite its interrogative form; Ibn Kathir, Qatada, and Ibn Muhaysin read without the interrogative hamza, apparently still implying a question.
rows.anchor: استفهام تقرير ولذلك أكد بإن واللام لأن التأكيد يقتضي التحقق المنافي للاستفهام الحقيقي

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وقتادة وابن محيصن
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Qatada, and Ibn Muhaysin read إنك without the interrogative hamza; al-Bahr finds a question still implied, while a plain assertion is unlikely unless different speakers' words were combined.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وقتادة وابن محيصن ( إنك ) بغير همزة استفهام

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy's reading adds أو: 'Are you ... or are you Joseph?' Ibn Jinni and al-Zamakhshari supply an omitted predicate in different ways; al-Kashf prefers the lower-ellipsis version, while al-Tibi suggests the brothers contrast his known status with Joseph's identity.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي ( أئنك أو أنت يوسف ) وخرج ذلك ابن جني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In either main reading, أنت is the subject and يوسف its predicate, with their clause serving as the predicate of إن; أنت cannot emphasize إن's pronoun because the lām intervenes.
rows.anchor: في القراءتين مبتدأ و ( يوسف ) خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suggested ways the brothers recognized Joseph include his features and bearing, seeing him after he drew them near, hearing him after a curtain was raised, recognizing his pearl-like shining teeth when he smiled, or seeing a birthmark shared with Jacob, Isaac, and Sarah; his speech also sounded Abrahamic and Muslim.
rows.anchor: عرفوه بروائه وشمائله وكان قد أدناهم اليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say they only guessed and did not recognize him until he identified himself; Al-Alusi says the earlier recognition explanations are the relied-upon view.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أنهم انما قالوا ذلك على التوهم ولم يعرفوه حتى أخبر عن نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph answers directly, then calls the second man his brother from both parents to further establish his identity; one reading treats this as a wise redirection to God's favor, while another sees it as completing the answer about what befell Joseph and his brother.
rows.anchor: مبالغة في تعريف نفسه

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Irshad reads 'God has favored us' as rescue from trial, reunion after separation, honor after humiliation, and intimacy after estrangement, completing the brothers' earlier question about what they did to Joseph and his brother.
rows.anchor: فأنا يوسف وهذا أخي قد من الله تعالى علينا بالخلاص عما ابتليناه والاجتماع بعد الفرقة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One explanation sees Joseph's mention of his brother as an answer to their demand that Benjamin be returned: Benjamin is Joseph's brother, not theirs, so they have no claim to him.
rows.anchor: بأنه أخي لاأخوكم فلا وجه لطلبكم

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa treats قد من الله علينا as a new independent sentence; another parses it as a circumstantial clause, but Al-Alusi finds that difficult because هذا points to one person while علينا refers to both and the needed governor is absent.
rows.anchor: وجملة ( قد من ) الخ عند أبي البقاء مستأنفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in 'God does not waste their reward' refers to the doers of good; using the explicit noun instead of a pronoun signals that people of taqwa and patience are also people of ihsan, and the sentence gives the reason for God's favor.
rows.anchor: أي أجرهم وإنما وضع المظهر موضع المضمر تنبيها على أن المنعوتين بالتقوى والصبر موصوفون بالإحسان

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan declines to restrict taqwa and patience to a single form of conduct.
rows.anchor: واختار أبو حيان عدم التخصيص في التقوى والصبر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets taqwa as refraining from sin and patience as enduring prison.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد المراد من يتق في ترك المعصية ويصبر في السجن

rows.speaker: النخعي
rows.claim: Al-Nakha'i interprets taqwa as avoiding adultery and patience as enduring celibacy.
rows.anchor: والنخعي من يتق الزنا ويصبر على العزوبة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another interpretation is avoiding sins and bearing people's harm.
rows.anchor: من يتق المعاصي ويصبر على أذى الناس

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes the qualities as fearing God, refraining from sins, and persevering in both duties and avoiding prohibitions; al-Fara'id objects that taqwa can keep its literal sense of guarding against neglected commands and forbidden acts.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : المراد من يخف الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الفرائد
rows.claim: Al-Fara'id says taqwa should retain its literal meaning of avoiding omissions of duties and violations, while patience concerns involuntary hardships; patience may be the specific after the general or mean remaining steadfast in taqwa.
rows.anchor: من يحترز عن ترك ماأمر به وارتكاب مانهى عنه

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Tibi reads the statement as rebuking Joseph's brothers for not fearing God or patiently obeying God and their father; an objection says the other interpretation conveys the same admonition, which Al-Alusi questions.
rows.anchor: بأن هذه الجملة تعليل لما تقدم وتعريض باخوته بأنهم لم يخافوا عقابه تعالى

rows.speaker: قنبل
rows.claim: Qunbul reads يتقي with an extra yā; grammarians propose an emphatic yā with jussive, deletion of an estimated vowel, a nominative relative reading, or a silent final rā in يصبر. Al-Bahr prefers the rare dialectal jussive, also attested in prose despite Abu Ali's restriction to poetry.
rows.anchor: وقرأ قنبل ( من يتقي ) باثبات الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caravan leaves from the town of al-Arish in Egypt toward Jacob, who is near Jerusalem; the claim that Jacob lived in al-Jazira is not reliable.
rows.anchor: خرجت من عريش مصر قاصدة مكان يعقوب عليه السلام وكان قريبا من بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intransitive فصل means to depart a town and cross its walls, while transitive فصل means to separate something; Ibn Abbas reads انفصل العير.
rows.anchor: وجاوز حيطانه وهو لازم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reads ولما انفصل العير, 'when the caravan separated/departed'.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ( ولما انفصل العير )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob says he smells Yusuf's scent; God let him smell the scent clinging to the shirt from eight days' travel away according to Ibn Abbas, eighty parasangs according to Hasan and Ibn Jurayj, thirty days in another Hasan report, or ten nights in another.
rows.anchor: أي لأشم فهو وجود حاسة الشم أشمه الله تعالى ما عبق بالقميص من ريح يوسف

rows.speaker: أبو أيوب الهروي
rows.claim: Abu Ayyub al-Harawi reports that the wind asked permission to carry Yusuf's fragrance and God permitted it; Mujahid says the shirt's fragrance was from Paradise and reached Jacob, though Al-Alusi finds this attribution weaker than the direct link to Yusuf.
rows.anchor: وقد استأذنت الريح على ما روى عن أبي أيوب الهروي في إيصال عرف يوسف عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تفندون means to accuse someone of foolishness or corrupt judgment, especially senility; the word derives from fand, stone, as if the accused were made stone-like in understanding.
rows.anchor: أي تنسبوني إلى الفند بفتحتين ويستعمل بمعنى الفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poetic lines use الفند for folly and rebuke; أفند الدهر فلانا means age ruined him, while مفند describes an old man whose judgment has failed.
rows.anchor: وجاء أفند الدهر فلانا أفسده

rows.speaker: الجوهري وغيره
rows.claim: Al-Jawhari and other lexicographers say one calls an old man مفند, but not an old woman مفندة, since she supposedly had no judgment even in youth; al-Samin calls this odd, and Al-Alusi suggests women's intellect exists but declines with age.
rows.anchor: عجوز مفندة لأنها لارأي لها في شبيبتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The جواب of لولا is omitted; possible completions are that his family would have believed him, or he would have said Joseph was near or would soon return.
rows.anchor: إن يوسف قريب مكانه أو لقاؤه أو نحو ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The addressees are identified either as the many sons who stayed behind when the others went to procure provisions, or as Jacob's grandchildren and relatives present with him; the latter is the common view.
rows.anchor: ولد ولده ومن كان بحضرته من ذوي قرابته وهو المشهور
